summary: Comprehensive backend API testing for Cricket Academy app. All 33 pytest cases passed (100% success). Covered auth (register/login/me/logout/refresh/brute-force), seeded public data (lanes=5, coaches=3, games=2, awards=4), bookings (CRUD, 24h rule, conflict, availability), 1-1 sessions (day/hours validation, conflict), progress reports (admin creates, user sees + notified), games + mocked email/whatsapp/in-app notify, announcements, notifications (list + mark read), and role-based access control (user/coach can't hit admin endpoints).

minor.issue: allow_origin_regex='.*' combined with allow_credentials=True; browsers will still reject. The `origins` list is computed but never passed to CORSMiddleware. Should pass allow_origins=origins instead of allow_origin_regex='.*'.
Fine for HTTPS prod, but will break cookie-based auth in any plain http dev environment.
For coach role, query filters by user['coach_id'] which is never set on the coach user doc — coach will always see zero sessions. Need to link coach user to coach record.
Does not re-validate new_hour/new_dur are inside 6-22 business hours; user could move a booking to hour 3 or end at 23 via update.
parse_booking_dt treats booking as UTC, while 'past' check also uses UTC. Timezone of academy is unclear — bookings labelled '10:00' are actually 10:00 UTC, which could confuse users in different tz.
FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated; should migrate to lifespan handler.
No password complexity validation (only min_length=6). Also returns only public_user with no explicit 201 status (uses default 200).
Uses IP:email as key — trivially bypassed by rotating IPs. Consider per-email lockout too. Current behavior passes the basic test case.

action_items: Fix CORS: replace allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_origins=origins (include FRONTEND_URL) so credentialed requests actually work in browsers.
Link coach-user to their coach_id (either on seed or by email) so GET /api/sessions works for coach role.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1000 lines single-file — acceptable for MVP but should be split into routers/models/services modules for scale.
CORS: allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True is browser-rejected. The computed `origins` list is dead code.
Coach role bug: GET /api/sessions filters by user['coach_id'] which is never set during coach seeding.
PUT /api/bookings does not validate start_hour/duration remain within 6-22.
Deprecated on_event hooks — use lifespan context manager.
Timezone ambiguity: bookings stored in UTC but hours are treated as local — document or store tz-aware.
test_credentials: admin@cricketacademy.com / Admin@12345 | user@cricketacademy.com / User@12345 | coach@cricketacademy.com / Coach@12345 — all verified working
seed_data_creation: Seed data is auto-created in server.py startup (5 lanes, 3 coaches, 2 games, 4 awards, admin/user/coach users). Tests confirmed all seeded entities exist. Tests also created TEST_-prefixed transient bookings/sessions/progress/games/announcements; most were cancelled/deleted in-test. A few TEST_ progress/announcement/notification rows remain (not cleaned up by tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully green on 33 pytest cases via /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. Review comments above flag a likely real bug: CORS credentials config + coach's GET /api/sessions will appear broken in the UI when the main agent tests coach dashboards. Test file is reusable as regression suite — just re-run `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`.
rca of the issue: No bugs caused test failures. Code review RCA for CORS: allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True → Chrome/Firefox strip credentials; the code builds `origins` list but never passes it to CORSMiddleware. Fix: pass allow_origins=origins. RCA for coach-sessions: seed_coach_user creates a user with role=coach but no coach_id field; all_sessions() filters by user.get('coach_id') which is None → empty result. Fix: set coach_id on the coach user to match the seeded coach record (e.g., Vikram Rathore), or change filter to user['id'].
